skill.name: workflow-patterns

skill.summary: Apply TDD phases, checkpoint approvals, Git conventions, and verification gates to implementation tasks.

content.value_statement: Implementation tasks often lose traceability when testing, commits, and approvals follow inconsistent practices. This skill provides a repeatable TDD workflow with checkpoints, Git guidance, and verification gates.
actual_capabilities: Structure work into red, green, and refactor TDD stages.
Guide sequential task selection from a phase plan.
Define checkpoint verification and approval requirements.
Recommend focused Git commits, notes, and plan updates.
Cover testing, coverage, linting, type safety, and documentation gates.
limitations: It does not run tests, coverage tools, linters, or type checkers.
It does not inspect a repository unless the user provides relevant context.
Its examples use generic project names and require adaptation.
It cannot replace environment-specific validation or expert review.

use_cases.title: Plan a feature with TDD
use_cases.description: Break a feature into ordered tasks with failing tests, minimal implementation, refactoring, and acceptance checks.

use_cases.title: Run a phase checkpoint
use_cases.description: Review automated and manual verification evidence before requesting approval for the next implementation phase.

use_cases.title: Document implementation history
use_cases.description: Create focused commit messages, Git notes, plan updates, and deviation records that preserve project context.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic TDD plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a beginner-friendly TDD plan for a small feature. Include red, green, and refactor steps plus clear acceptance checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when starting a small feature without an implementation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Order implementation tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this task list into a Conductor-style workflow. Identify the next task, required tests, implementation steps, and completion evidence: [paste task list]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when a project has several pending tasks in one phase.

prompt_templates.title: Review phase readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this completed phase against the workflow. Check tests, coverage, linting, documentation, type safety, and approval requirements: [paste artifacts]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this before presenting a phase checkpoint for approval.

prompt_templates.title: Design a multi-phase workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-phase implementation plan for [project]. Define task order, checkpoint criteria, commit structure, deviation handling, and recovery steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a complex project that needs explicit controls across multiple phases.

output_examples.input: A feature request for email validation with no existing test plan.
output_examples.output: An ordered TDD plan starts with valid, invalid, and error-condition tests, then defines the smallest implementation and a refactoring review.

output_examples.input: A completed phase with tests passing, 78% coverage, and no approval record.
output_examples.output: The review identifies coverage below the 80% target and missing approval evidence. It recommends adding tests, rerunning verification, and requesting explicit approval.

best_practices: Write failing tests before implementation and keep the first implementation minimal.
Use focused commits and update the plan immediately after task completion.
Require automated checks and explicit approval before creating a phase checkpoint.
anti_patterns: Skipping the red phase and writing implementation before defining behavior.
Combining unrelated changes into one commit without task or phase context.
Proceeding after a checkpoint without reviewing failures or receiving approval.

faq.question: What workflow does this skill describe?
faq.answer: It describes a Conductor-style workflow built around TDD stages, sequential tasks, phase checkpoints, and verification gates.

faq.question: Does this skill execute tests or Git commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Your development environment must run commands and confirm their results.

faq.question: What should happen during the red phase?
faq.answer: Write tests that describe expected behavior, including successful paths, edge cases, and error conditions, then confirm they fail.

faq.question: When should a phase checkpoint be created?
faq.answer: Create one after phase tasks and verification steps are complete, then record approval and the checkpoint commit.

faq.question: How does the workflow handle deviations?
faq.answer: Record the deviation, reason, and impact in the project documentation, then update the plan or technical documentation when needed.

faq.question: Can this replace project-specific review?
faq.answer: No. It supplies a repeatable process, but teams must still perform environment-specific testing, security review, and expert validation.
